The brain is not that different from an artificial intelligence. It needs to be trained in order to be useful. Nearly everything that you experience influences how your brain is wired. We did not evolve to be perfect thinkers because being successful, from evolution's perspective, does not demand it. In many cases, perfect thinking would get in the way of that success. This is why we still have instincts. They contradict our rational thinking for the benefit of this success. This article about cognitive bias describes types of cognitive biases. While it is presented as ways our brains error from being rational, it is better to think of this as a list of how our brains work, since being rational is something that evolution rarely selects for.

Since we all have different experiences, we are all going to build a different map of the world in our heads. The map is not the territory. Genetics, diseases, food, and drugs affect the mechanics of the brain. However, the information within it comes from our unique experiences. Our different maps (our mental representation) of reality (the territory) means that we interpret events differently than everyone else.

I recommend Scott Adam's discussions on persuasion for practical applications of this.
